concepts.def: Releases energy to the surroundings, often as heat; surroundings get hotter.
Reactants higher than products in an exothermic reaction; difference is energy released.
Energy needed to break (or released forming) one mole of a particular bond.
Releases energy; if more energy released making bonds than breaking, reaction is exothermic.
Combustion, neutralisation, many oxidation reactions, hand warmers.
ΔH is negative for an exothermic reaction.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Chemical Energetics — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Chemical Energetics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Chemical Energetics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
